### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa6a6085c07df22274fa56bfc93141f75f50d25b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e1ebfa83dec261cd58036814744dab3a1b2ae035` — the merge of head `47cec88f799788a248f429dded7762dbb7bea40c` into base `fa6a6085c07df22274fa56bfc93141f75f50d25b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e1ebfa83dec261cd58036814744dab3a1b2ae035 && git checkout e1ebfa83dec261cd58036814744dab3a1b2ae035
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa6a6085c07df22274fa56bfc93141f75f50d25b 47cec88f799788a248f429dded7762dbb7bea40c && git checkout -B drift-repro fa6a6085c07df22274fa56bfc93141f75f50d25b && git merge --no-ff 47cec88f799788a248f429dded7762dbb7bea40c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa6a6085c07df22274fa56bfc93141f75f50d25b
```

</details>

## 席位复核: REWORK, patch round 1 (two items) · 2026-10-15T01:17Z

`domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `sunhaolin` · `session_01Q9PZ5Pzqcus4woVvTZwWNU` · reviewed head `cac34a830d`, against `origin/main` `cdc42eb495`. Same claim (`6180949086`), same dev, by SendMessage.

**What holds (read on GitHub, not from the report):**
- `walledBindingRemedy` and the posture branch in `verifyReferences` (the only source change).
- The single-posture pointer, the uncomposed-plugin remedy (still asked first) and the `conflicting` text are unchanged.
- The gate still refuses.
- The served pin measures a code declaration clearing the gate and `zz_shipped` getting the sealed fact.
- The dynamic import of `@objectstack/metadata-core` stands, because PR #23461 (open) holds the import region.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main` is clean.

**Item 1: the undeclared remedy contradicts itself. The error is this seat's.**
- **What the text says:** "Declare the position NAME in the environment catalog with permissionSets naming SETS, through one door only: the deployment's code (compiled into the artifact this ceremony boots), or the metadata door …".
- **Why that is wrong:** in this codebase, the environment catalog is the environment-authored items hydrated from `sys_metadata` (`standalone-stack-security-catalog-one-holder.test.ts:170`). The remedy's own next sentence uses it that way: "a position name a package declares and the environment catalog also holds". A code declaration is a package declaration, so "in the environment catalog … through the deployment's code" says two opposite things.
- **Where it came from:** this seat's readings review `6180941823` wrote "declare the position in the environment catalog … A1: the deployment's code". The dev followed it.
- **The shipped release text** (`.changeset/pre/15204-s1-position-permission-sets.md:50`) has no such phrase: "declare the binding in the position's `permissionSets` through the metadata door … or in the app's code".
- **Fix:** drop "in the environment catalog" from that sentence, and from the same sentence in the changeset's TO line and the PR body's table.

**Item 2: one unit pin asserts an act the real door forbids.**
- **The pin:** in the uncomposed-block test, `expect(blockerOf(rewrite, 'position everyone ')).toContain('PUT /api/v1/meta/position/everyone')`.
- **Why it is wrong:** it passes only because the helper's default lock stub answers `editable: true`. This PR's served boot measured `everyone` as `editable: false`, `lock: no-overlay`, so the real remedy is the sealed fact, with no act.
- **Fix:** either give that case the door's served answer and assert the fact with no act, or assert only that the pointer and the composition are gone.

Everything else is unchanged.

- **Changeset prose, sentence by sentence:** `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, `fix(cli):`, `Clause-②: no`.

All 8 skips are roster names: Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance.
